title: Event telemetry retention and pipeline implementation notes
content:
Purpose and scope:

This doc captures implementation notes for audit/event telemetry retention and the supporting pipelines. It focuses on storage tiering, index/mapping choices, backfill orchestration, failure-mode handling, and the cross-cutting concerns of RBAC v2, evidence automation, and SIEM export. This is an operational/engineering working doc — expect TODOs and rough commands.

Goals / non-goals:
- Ensure tamper-evident, queryable audit data for security/compliance cases.
- Meet retention SLAs: hot (90d), warm (2 years), cold (7 years) for regulated customers; default hosted tier 1 year.
- Provide reliable SIEM-friendly exports (near-real-time + batch).
- Make backfills and reindex safe, idempotent, and observable.
- NOT covering access request workflows or legal hold workflow details (separate playbook).

High-level architecture summary:
- Ingest -> validation & enrichment -> primary index (hot) -> indexing tiering pipeline -> cold archival (object store) -> SIEM export layer / evidence automation hooks.
- Primary systems: Kafka for ingest buffer, Elasticsearch/OpenSearch for hot/warm indexes, GCS/S3 for cold blobs, Dataflow/Beam or K8s workers for backfills and rehydration, and a small metadata DB (Postgres) to track archival manifests and evidence markers.

Schema and indexing notes:
- Core audit event fields (flat schema; keep small, typed): event_id (uuid), timestamp (ISO8601), principal_id, principal_type, action, resource_type, resource_id, client_ip, request_id, request_payload_hash, outcome (success|failure), rbac_version (string), rbac_changes (json-string for diff), cluster_region, ingest_shard, retention_tier.
- Avoid deeply nested objects in primary index to keep mappings stable. When we need structured details, keep them as compressed JSON string fields (e.g., request_metadata_blob) and extract the few searchable fields we need (user, resource, action).
- Index naming: events-hot-YYYYMM, events-warm-YYYY, archive-manifests-YYYY. Monthly hot indices allow targeted reindex window and shard sizing.
- Mapping choices: set event_id keyword, timestamp date with strict format, principal_id keyword, action keyword, resource_type keyword, outcome keyword, request_payload_hash keyword. Use ingest pipeline to populate a synthetic search_field (lowercased concat of principal, action, resource) to enable cheap full-text style filtering without large mappings.
- Estimated avg doc size: 1.5KB. Shard sizing: target 30–40GB primary shard for hot indices, 1 replica for durability. Start with 3 primaries for the monthly index, adjust by ingestion QPS.

Retention tiering & transitions:
- Hot (0-90d): low-latency indices in ES/OpenSearch, frequent refresh.
- Warm (90d-2y): reindex into a warmer cluster with reduced replicas and segment merging policies. Optimize for slower queries (e.g., audit search UI).
- Cold (2y+ up to 7y): store as compressed NDJSON gz blobs in object store with an index manifest in Postgres that lists (event_id -> blob, offset). Cold retrieval path supports legal/evidence requests; rehydrate to warm if queried.
- TTL enforcement: use scheduled job (daily) to mark documents exceeding retention for archival and deletion; never auto-delete without manifest and evidence flag checks.

Evidence automation hooks & RBAC v2 implications:
- Evidence automation must tag events relevant to evidence collections early in ingest (evidence_flag) and copy manifests to a tamper-evident store (HSM-backed audit manifests are an enhancement).
- RBAC v2 adds fields to events: rbac_version, policy_id, decision_reason. Ensure these fields are present in hot index; they are crucial for forensic timelines.
- Access controls: only security/audit service accounts can read cold manifests; UI access to warm/hot must respect RBAC v2 derived privileges (enforce via proxy layer that consults RBAC service).

SIEM export considerations:
- Two export paths: streaming (for high-priority events) and batch (hourly/daily aggregates). Streaming uses Kafka sink connectors that transform into vendor schema (CEF/LEEF/JSON) and forward to SIEM. Batch exports generate gzipped NDJSON slices and post to customer S3/HTTP endpoint with retry/backoff.
- Keep exported payloads small: exclude large payload blobs unless explicitly requested. Use request_payload_hash to map to blob store when SIEM needs full context.
- Rate-limiting: configurable per-customer export throttle. Backpressure from SIEM endpoints must not block ingest; use durable queues and dead-letter topics.

Backfills, reindexing and rehydration strategy:
- Common triggers: mapping update requiring reindex, warm->hot compaction, evidence rehydration for investigations, customer retention policy change (e.g., extend to 7 years).
- Orchestration tool: adopt a small controller (k8s CRD or Dataflow job manager) that creates a backfill plan broken into granular ranges (by time window and shard). Each unit is idempotent and records status to Postgres manifest per unit (pending/running/succeeded/failed).
- Safe reindex pattern: read from source index via slice, write to target index with write-ahead manifest entry; once slice done and verified (doc counts + sample hash), commit and update routing. Use zero-downtime alias swap for readers.
- Rehydration flow (cold->warm): read blob manifest, stream events into warm reindex job, validate checksums, mark rehydrated flag in manifest. Allow partial rehydrates and resume by offset.

Failure modes and runbook snippets:
1) Ingest lag/backpressure (Kafka consumer lag grows):
   - Symptoms: hot index lag, metrics: kafka_consumer_lag > threshold, queue_depth rising.
   - Immediate actions: scale consumer replicas by 2x, enable temporary burst instances, increase consumer parallelism (slices).
   - Root causes: downstream ES write throttling, network egress spikes, slow enrichment service.
   - Postmortem items: increase write thread pool, add circuit breaker for enrichment, create backpressure-aware buffer with longer retention.

2) Corrupted index shard after reindex attempt:
   - Symptoms: indexing errors referencing mapper_parsing_exception, checksum mismatches.
   - Actions: fail job, restore shard snapshot from last successful snapshot, mark offending units for manual inspection.
   - Preventive: validate mapping changes in staging with full reindex simulation and sample checksums.

3) Cold blob store missing objects (object not found during rehydrate):
   - Symptoms: rehydrate job fails with object-not-found, manifests referencing missing offsets.
   - Actions: consult object-store access logs, attempt re-replication from backup, escalate to storage infra. Mark affected manifests as degraded and collect meta for compliance.
   - Preventive: periodic manifest vs object-store reconciliation job, run weekly.

4) SIEM export failures due to endpoint throttling:
   - Symptoms: sink connector errors, DLQ growth.
   - Actions: pause exports for affected customer, retry with exponential backoff, notify customer ops with details and ETA.

Observability and SLOs:
- Key metrics to emit: ingest_p99_latency, index_write_failures, kafka_consumer_lag, backfill_failure_rate, rehydrate_success_rate, export_dropped_events.
- Dashboards: per-tenant ingestion heatmap, hot/warm index sizes and shard counts, backfill job queue, cold manifest reconciliation status.
- SLO examples: ingest-to-index latency 99th <= 30s for hosted tier; archival manifest creation within 2h after TTL crossing.

Security and tamper-evidence:
- Signed manifests: each daily archive manifest should be cryptographically signed (private key guarded by HSM/KMS). Store signatures separately and log signature events to audit index.
- Immutable archival: cold blobs write-once policy with object-store versioning enabled. Disable delete for archive prefix except via authorized legal workflow.

Operational checklists (quick):
- Deploy mapping change: 1) stage mapping in test cluster, 2) run full reindex simulation, 3) create backfill plan, 4) execute reindex with small slices, 5) monitor digest hashes, 6) alias swap, 7) snapshot target index.
- Run recovery for failed rehydrate: 1) pause downstream queries, 2) identify missing blobs via manifest checks, 3) try object-store recovery, 4) if unrecoverable, notify compliance and provide affected event range.

Open items / TODOs:
- Define retention policy variants per region/customer and integrate into billing/contracting flows (who owns longer retention cost).
- Add HSM signature pipeline for manifests (design + PoC).
- Harden RBAC v2 fields in ingest path: make rbac changes a separate small index for fast policy audits.
- Add automatic manifest vs object-store weekly reconciliation job and alerting when divergence > 0.01%.

References and quick links:
- Confluence: SEC logs lifecycle (linked above)
- Jira: JIRA-SEC-4321 (RBAC v2 ingest work)
- GitHub: audit-ingest repo (linked above)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally operational and prescriptive. Lean on infra and security leads for shard sizing and HSM decisions. I expect mapping choices and shard counts to be iterated after load tests.

-- Maya
